- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes (especially >0.23), especially when recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices after strong negative sentiment (e.g., sentiment < -0.16) or after a sharp drop, particularly if the model ignores recent downward momentum.
- Model tends to overreact to recent price spikes, overshooting by 2–5% in the next 3–5 days; apply a 1–2% downward correction after a spike.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model often fails to account for mean reversion; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until price stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to first 5 days.
- If sentiment is positive but recent price is falling, model often ignores the trend; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model tends to overestimate the peak; cap forecast at 1–2% below the 5-day moving average of recent highs.
